title: Canonical diagonal assembly and affine-target restriction data
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum $P$ of [def-pur-conventions], the ordinary and compared dualizing objects of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object], the section invariant [def-pur-section-invariant], and the canonical coefficient twists and transport $t$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Morphism properties have the meanings of [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and pure-dimensional smoothness has the meaning of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. This definition re-exports three existing constructions used in target-open descent, without asserting the normalization or existence conclusions of an affine-target theorem.

First, for schemes $U,V$, $d\in\mathbf N$, a separated, locally finite type, quasi-compact morphism $h:U\to V$ smooth of pure relative dimension $d$, and a locally finite type, quasi-compact structure map $a_V:V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ with $a_V\circ h$ separated, define the diagonal assembly to be the existing canonical composite $\alpha_h^{-1}\circledast\delta_h\circledast\beta_h$ (composition in the displayed order). Here $\alpha_h$ is the canonical diagonal comparison of [def-pur-diagonal-dnc-chart-data], $\delta_h$ is the uniquely coordinate-normalized DNC comparison of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance], and $\beta_h$ is normal-cone comparison followed by restriction of the specified projection orientation and its Tate transport, as in [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity]. The Lean abbreviation is definitionally the published chartDiagonalAssembly, not a second construction.

Second, for a separated, locally finite type, quasi-compact smooth $f:X\to Y$ of pure relative dimension $d$ and a locally finite type, quasi-compact structure map $a_Y:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, and an arbitrary Cartesian square with maps $b:Y'\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $a:X'\to X$, where $f'$ is compactifiable [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and quasi-compact, define the ordinary base-change isomorphism $a^*\omega_f\simeq\omega_{f'}$. It is the existing chartOrdinaryBaseChange: pullback of the inverse coefficient-unit comparison, the actual smooth exceptional base-change mate of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness], and the coefficient-unit comparison for $f'$. Pullback is the one in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. No separatedness of $Y$ over $k$ is assumed.

Third, for arbitrary $f:X\to Y$, $a_Y:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $d\in\mathbf N$ and affine open $V\subset Y$, define the affine geometry dictionary to be exactly the existing AffineDiagonalGeometry. Its fields assert separatedness, local finite type, quasi-compactness and smoothness of pure dimension $d$ for $h=f|_V:f^{-1}V\to V$; local finite type and quasi-compactness for $V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; separatedness, local finite type and quasi-compactness over $k$ for both $f^{-1}V$ and its actual self-product over $V$ (using the first projection). This is a dictionary of proposition instances, not a claim that such a dictionary exists. All three abbreviations include $d=0$ and empty schemes. They copy no data and use exactly the original constructions.
